comparison: Perfect agreement on guinea pig model validity (C7-C9, C34-C36, C109-C113). Both evaluations affirm the model as a strength, with peer reviewers explicitly noting similarity to human Ca2+ handling and ionic currents. OpenEval and peer reviews both cite supporting literature and established knowledge.

Perfect agreement on echocardiographic findings (C40-C43, C126-C129). Both evaluations support structural and functional preservation with DS treatment. Peer reviewers describe data as 'convincing' with 'validated methodology,' matching OpenEval's assessment of quantitative data with appropriate statistics.

Strong agreement on primary efficacy outcomes (C37-C39, C122-C125). Both evaluations affirm arrhythmia reduction and survival improvements. Peer reviewers explicitly state findings are 'convincing' and 'clearly demonstrate positive effects,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of statistical significance and adequate sample sizes. OpenEval includes C10 while peer review does not.

Agreement on molecular mechanisms (C48, C97, C130-C135, C150-C151). Both evaluations support findings on RyR2 oxidation and Ca2+ handling. Peer reviewers affirm the mechanistic story without raising concerns about molecular measurements, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of quantitative evidence and appropriate statistics.

Agreement on fibrosis findings (C44-C46). Both evaluations support reduced fibrosis with DS treatment. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'reduced fibrosis' as a key outcome with 'convincing' data. OpenEval includes C47 and peer review includes C98, showing slight variation in scope but consistent support.

Agreement on heart rate and functional outcomes (C11, C49-C52, C136-C137). Both evaluations support these findings. Peer reviewers note 'convincing' ECG data demonstrating positive effects. Peer review R3 covers broader functional outcomes (C12-C14, C53-C55, C75, C108, C138) beyond heart rate alone.

Agreement on QTc normalization (C56-C58, C141-C142). Both evaluations support ECG findings. Peer review R7 covers broader electrophysiological findings including QT variability (C59-C61, C74, C102, C143-C144) that OpenEval addresses separately in R14 and R15.

Agreement on QT variability findings (C59-C60, C143-C144). Both evaluations support reduced QT dispersion as mechanistically important. Peer review R7 groups these with broader electrophysiological findings, while OpenEval treats QT variability separately from QTc normalization.

Agreement on crossover study efficacy (C62-C66, C145-C149). Both evaluations support DS efficacy when started after HF development. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as 'important' showing 'improvements in function and decreased arrhythmogenesis.' OpenEval notes lack of statistical significance in one group as 'somewhat speculative.'

Agreement on crossover ECG findings (C69-C72, C152-C153, C155-C157). Both evaluations support reversibility of electrophysiological abnormalities. Peer review R8 covers broader crossover findings including functional recovery, while OpenEval focuses specifically on ECG parameters.

Agreement on PVC burden reversibility (C67-C68, C154). Both evaluations support findings from crossover study. OpenEval emphasizes reversibility with DS withdrawal/reinitiation supporting causality. Peer review R8 groups this with broader crossover findings.

Agreement on overall DS efficacy in prevention and reversal (C73, C76, C96, C101). Both evaluations support comprehensive conclusions. Peer reviewers treat reversibility of chronic HF as a key strength. OpenEval emphasizes evidence strength for 'reversal' based on functional recovery.

Agreement on molecular findings from crossover study (C150-C151). Both evaluations support DS reducing RyR2 oxidation regardless of timing. Peer review R6 groups this with broader molecular mechanisms, while OpenEval treats crossover molecular data separately.

Agreement on chronotropic response (C12, C53, C55, C75, C108). Both evaluations support restoration of chronotropic competence. Peer review R3 covers broader functional outcomes including heart rate and HRV. OpenEval notes mechanistic link to β-adrenergic signaling is 'somewhat inferential.'

Agreement on HRV findings (C13, C54, C138). Both evaluations support HRV improvements as important prognostic markers. Peer review R3 groups this with broader functional ECG data, while OpenEval treats HRV separately.

Agreement on improved cardiac function (C14, C18). Both evaluations support functional improvements. Peer review R3 covers broader functional outcomes. OpenEval emphasizes mechanistic interpretation linking SR Ca2+ load to contractility based on established physiology.

Agreement on mechanistic interpretation linking RyR2 inhibition to reduced repolarization lability (C16, C61, C107). Both evaluations support the mechanism. Peer review R9 covers broader mechanistic model (C15, C17-C18, C77, C96, C115) while noting 'some mechanistic details remain to be worked out.'

Agreement on mechanistic model linking oxidative stress, RyR2 hyperactivity, and arrhythmogenesis (C15, C77-C87). Both evaluations support the overall mechanism. Peer reviewers affirm the 'vicious cycle' interpretation while acknowledging details need further investigation. OpenEval emphasizes literature support and consistency with established knowledge.

Partial overlap on primary mechanistic findings (C10). OpenEval R5 focuses on mechanistic interpretation linking DS to VT/VF/SCD prevention (C10, C17, C74). Peer review R2 covers primary efficacy outcomes more broadly. Both support the findings.

Agreement on overarching conclusions (C114-C115). Both evaluations support comprehensive summary. Peer review R9 emphasizes mechanistic interpretation of breaking the 'vicious cycle,' while OpenEval emphasizes multiple lines of evidence supporting conclusions.

Disagreement on exclusion of female animals (C120-C121). OpenEval finds methods justified by sex differences in disease progression. Peer reviewers explicitly critique this as a weakness, noting 'considerable known sex differences in Ca2+ handling' and stating 'it will be very important to determine effects in the female heart.'

Agreement on structural findings and SR Ca2+ association with fibrosis (C98-C100). Both evaluations support structural improvements. OpenEval emphasizes mechanistic link between SR Ca2+ leak and fibrosis is incompletely understood. Peer review R5 focuses on reduced fibrosis outcome.

Agreement on electrophysiological phenotype of HF (C102-C106). Both evaluations support ECG findings and mechanistic basis. Peer review R7 groups this with broader electrophysiological data, while OpenEval treats the HF phenotype characterization separately.

OpenEval supports clinical context and rationale (C1-C3, C19-C24) as well-supported by clinical literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background/introduction claims.

OpenEval supports scientific rationale for targeting RyR2 (C4-C6, C25-C33) as well-supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background claims about RyR2 biology.

OpenEval supports pathophysiological context (C88-C92) as established knowledge about β-adrenergic signaling and Ca2+ handling. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background claims.

OpenEval supports findings from authors' previous work (C93-C95) linking oxidative stress to RyR2 dysfunction, citing Dey et al., 2018. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these prior findings.
OpenEval supports established knowledge about QT parameters as prognostic markers (C139-C140), citing literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background claims.
